data.reasoning: The PKGBUILD is standard, uses a pinned source with a SHA256 checksum, and standard build tools (meson, ninja). The only disagreement stems from transient API errors in the qwen model when reviewing non-executable metadata files (LICENSE, REUSE.toml). These files pose no security risk, and the deepseek model successfully reviewed them and found them safe.
data.disagreement_analysis: The qwen model experienced HTTP 400 API errors when auditing LICENSE and REUSE.toml, resulting in an 'inconclusive' overall verdict. The deepseek model successfully audited all files and returned 'safe'. The disagreement is purely due to a transient tool error, not a difference in security assessment.
coverage_issues: qwen model failed to audit LICENSE and REUSE.toml due to API errors, though these are non-executable files and do not impact the security verdict.
learnings: The audit tool should differentiate between security-critical files (PKGBUILD, .install, patches, scripts) and non-executable metadata (LICENSE, README, REUSE.toml). Transient API errors on non-executable files should not force an 'inconclusive' verdict if all critical files are successfully audited and found safe.
